title: General Manager
description:
An exciting new chapter is beginning at Budock Vean Hotel, and we’re looking for an exceptional General Manager to help lead it.

Set within 65 acres on the banks of Cornwall’s beautiful Helford River, Budock Vean is a hotel with a wonderful history, a loyal team and guests who return time and again. But we’re also looking firmly to the future.

Over the next few years, Budock Vean will enter an exciting period of investment and development, including the creation of a new spa, planned to open in spring/summer 2028. This represents an important next step for the hotel, building on everything our guests already love while creating an even stronger luxury leisure and wellness experience for the future.

We’re looking for a General Manager who is excited by the opportunity to be part of that journey. You’ll lead the hotel day to day, develop a brilliant and engaged team, drive commercial performance and exceptional guest experiences, while also playing an important role in preparing the hotel for its next chapter.

This isn’t simply a role maintaining what already exists. It’s an opportunity to help shape what Budock Vean becomes.

What we’re looking for

  • An experienced hotel leader with a strong understanding of full-service hotel operations
  • A visible, hands-on leader who enjoys being around guests and the team
  • Strong commercial awareness, with confidence around budgets, payroll, revenue and profitability
  • A genuine passion for developing people and building strong departmental leadership
  • A calm, practical approach and the ability to make good decisions
  • High standards with excellent attention to detail
  • A natural communicator who builds trust across all levels of the business
  • Experience of leading a hotel through change, development or significant investment would be particularly valuable
  • An interest in luxury hospitality, wellness and spa would be advantageous

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Lead the hotel operation, ensuring consistently high standards across accommodation, food and beverage, spa, leisure and the wider guest experience.
  • Be a visible and hands-on General Manager, building relationships with guests and the team and maintaining a strong presence throughout the hotel.
  • Create an exceptional guest experience, understanding what our guests value while continually looking for opportunities to improve and evolve what we offer.
  • Build, develop and retain a brilliant team, creating a positive working environment where people understand what is expected of them, feel supported and are encouraged to develop.
  • Develop strong departmental leaders, giving managers the confidence, accountability and support to lead their own areas effectively.
  • Drive the commercial performance of the hotel, with responsibility for revenue, profitability, payroll, budgets and effective cost control.
  • Identify opportunities to grow revenue and in-house spend across bedrooms, food and beverage, spa, leisure and experiences, without compromising the quality of the guest experience.
  • Work closely with the wider group teams, including Operations, Sales, Marketing, Revenue and Finance, to maximise the performance and positioning of Budock Vean.
  • Play an active role in preparing for the new spa opening in spring/summer 2028, helping to ensure the hotel, operation, guest journey and team are ready to make the most of this significant investment.
  • Help shape the future direction of Budock Vean, recognising and protecting what makes the hotel special while identifying where we can evolve and improve.
  • Maintain the hotel to a high standard, working proactively with maintenance and wider teams to identify priorities for repair, refurbishment and improvement.
  • Take ownership of guest feedback and complaints, resolving issues thoughtfully while using feedback to identify opportunities for longer-term improvement.
  • Ensure strong operational and financial controls, with accurate reporting and clear understanding of the hotel's performance.
  • Maintain excellent standards of compliance, including health and safety, fire safety, food safety and other statutory and company requirements.
  • Lead through change positively and practically, ensuring improvements are well considered, properly communicated and sustainable rather than short-term fixes.

title: Director of Project Management
description:
Total Comp: $120,000 - $180,000 Yearly (base + bonus)
Also Known As: Director of PMO
Location: Overland Park, KS
Company: DataMap
Client Work:

About DataMap

DataMap.ai is an AI-first technology consulting and solutions company focused on enterprise systems and automation. We build applications, implement ERP platforms, and provide managed services and production support at scale. Our clients include Fortune 500 enterprises and high-growth companies such as Google. They rely on us to modernize operations and automate workflows in ways that produce measurable business value.

DataMap is growing fast. We value innovation and collaboration, we work with urgency, and we reward speed, precision, and accountability. Teams here have the authority to solve complex enterprise problems and deliver results.

Why Join DataMap

At DataMap, projects run the way we expect every project to run in five years, with AI copilots drafting plans, surfacing risks, and writing first-draft status reports. You'll take that setup further by leading the AI transformation of project management across everything DataMap runs, working with DataMap's executive team.

You'll represent DataMap's AI-first delivery with client executives and at industry events, alongside Sales and executive leadership. The flagship AI and automation programs you lead are built on our proprietary products (Positron, RoboApprover, Itemova EDI SaaS) and on enterprise platforms such as Coupa, D365, NetSuite, SAP, and Boomi.

Role Overview

As the Director of Project Management, you lead the project management practice. Project management at DataMap owns the management of all of our work, which covers everything: customer work, partner work, partnership growth, internal projects, and operations projects. That work ranges from partner-platform implementations for enterprise clients and development of the products and customer portals we build and sell to the partnership-growth, internal, and operations projects that make DataMap itself run and grow. You are accountable for the health of the whole portfolio: every engagement and initiative delivered on time, on budget, and with the outcomes it promised. That accountability extends to the governance, standards, and quality gates the practice runs on, and to the PMO's utilization and margin and the growth that delivery generates. You chair executive steering committees and are the escalation point for delivery risk across the portfolio, bringing executive leadership in when needed. With DataMap's executive leadership, you set direction for the practice's methodology and team.

At DataMap, project managers manage the work, grow the accounts they serve, and lead their teams toward business results. Senior Project Managers expand those practices across programs, and you build them into the way the whole PMO runs. You lead others inside the PMO (Senior Project Managers, Project Managers, and coordinators) and outside it (the leaders and teams the work depends on in consulting, engineering, QA, and managed services). You partner with Sales and client executives to keep the portfolio pointed at shared outcomes, and you drive change at the organization level in process, structure, visibility, communications, and change management.

You will use AI tools every day and lead the AI transformation of the PMO with the executive team.

Your Growth Path

Project management at DataMap has a defined five-level ladder that runs from delivery support to leading the practice: Project Coordinator, Senior Project Coordinator, Project Manager, Senior Project Manager, and Director of Project Management. We post every level and promote from within, and moving up depends on performance and on the needs of the business. Beyond the Director level, the path continues into executive leadership, such as DataMap's Vice President, Operations & Delivery.

This is the top of the project management ladder: you are accountable for the management of everything DataMap runs, and you lead the practice, its people, and its methodology in partnership with executive leadership. The Vice President, Operations & Delivery is part of DataMap's executive team, leads operational strategy and delivery performance, and connects Sales, Delivery, Product, and Support. Directors who show they can lead beyond their own practice may be considered for executive roles like it.

Key Responsibilities

Practice and portfolio leadership

  • Lead the management of all of DataMap's work (customer, partner, partnership-growth, internal, and operations work alike), and be accountable for portfolio health, including schedule, margin, quality, and outcomes.
  • Lead the PMO's Senior Project Managers, Project Managers, and coordinators, and set the standard for how every project is run, led, and grown.
  • Lead outside the PMO as well: bring consulting, engineering, QA, and managed services together around shared priorities, decisions, and outcomes, and partner with Sales and client executives.
  • Chair executive steering committees, be the escalation point for engagements at delivery, commercial, or relationship risk, bring executive leadership in when needed, and maintain executive relationships across strategic accounts.

Change, process, and structure

  • Drive organization-level change in process, structure, visibility, communications, and change management. Diagnose what slows the practice down, set the direction, and drive the change management that makes each practice-wide shift in methodology, tooling, or structure hold.
  • Set and maintain the delivery standards, governance, and quality gates every project follows from kickoff to close, drawing on established practice such as PMI's.
  • Design the PMO's structure and operating cadence: roles, decision rights, escalation paths, portfolio reviews, and the handoffs between delivery, Sales, engineering, and managed services.
  • Run portfolio intake, prioritization, and health reviews, build portfolio reporting (health metrics, dashboards, and early warnings), and manage delivery communications so leadership, teams, and clients work from the same information.

Commercial and team

  • Be accountable for the PMO's commercial results: portfolio margin, utilization, forecasting, change-order discipline, and the expansion revenue that delivery generates through new software and service sales across Positron, RoboApprover, Itemova EDI SaaS, partner platforms, and follow-on services.
  • Build the lead-to-signature process every project manager runs, with the playbooks and pipeline reporting behind it, so that on active engagements project managers identify leads for new software and service sales, draft the orders (order forms, change orders, and SOW amendments), and get customer signatures.
  • Partner with Sales on pipeline, pursuits, and operationally achievable commitments, and contribute to the pricing and packaging of DataMap's delivery services.
  • Build the project management team: hiring, onboarding and training, the career ladder, and culture.
  • Develop the practice's next generation of leaders, coaching them to proactively engage team members, ask what they're working on, suggest course corrections, and drive business outcomes.

AI-first transformation

  • Lead the AI transformation of DataMap's PMO and the way it manages every type of work, including tool selection, methodology evolution, and ROI measurement, with the executive team.
  • Set the standard for AI-assisted delivery, including prompt libraries, workflow automation, and AI-driven early warnings on risk and margin, and measure the results in cycle time, quality, and margin.
  • Represent DataMap's AI-first delivery in client executive briefings, industry content and speaking, and pursuit support, and lead flagship AI and automation programs built on DataMap's own products.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of project delivery experience, including leading project managers and holding portfolio- or PMO-level responsibility.
  • A track record of organization-level change: transformations in process, structure, visibility, and communications that you led to completion and that held, with working knowledge of a structured change management approach.
  • A vision for the AI transformation of a delivery organization or PMO, and a track record of carrying one out.
  • Proven success chairing steering committees, advising C-level client stakeholders, and leading leaders outside your reporting line.
  • Commercial leadership experience with portfolio margin, utilization, forecasting, pricing input, and growing revenue through delivery, including building a delivery-led process that turns project leads into signed orders.
  • Demonstrated success building and developing project management teams: hiring, career paths, standards, and mentoring.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred Experience

  • PMP certification or equivalent experience (PgMP or PfMP a plus).
  • Consulting or professional services delivery leadership.
  • SaaS and ERP implementations (e.g., Coupa, NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, Salesforce) and integration platforms such as Boomi; Source-to-Pay or procurement depth.
  • Experience designing a PMO operating model: governance, portfolio reporting, and a career ladder.
  • Experience selecting and deploying AI tooling across a delivery organization, with measured ROI.
  • Familiarity with established change models such as Lewin's change model and Kotter's 8 steps; Prosci's ADKAR model, the Bridges Transition Model, or the McKinsey 7-S Framework a plus.
  • Public thought leadership: speaking, publishing, or community leadership in project delivery or applied AI.

Benefits & Perks

  • Total compensation of base salary plus bonus.
  • Unlimited vacation and a flexible work environment.
  • Free catered lunch on Fridays at headquarters.
  • On-site gym at headquarters.
  • 401(k) with employer match.
  • Health insurance with generous employer contribution.
  • Dental, life, and disability insurance.
  • Hands-on mentorship and career development opportunities.

Why Apply?

  • Lead the AI transformation of an enterprise delivery practice, working with DataMap's executive team and its own AI products.
  • Run a portfolio built on AI copilots and major financial and supply chain systems, and deliver AI programs for enterprise clients.
  • Work at a company that values innovation, collaboration, and professional growth.

If you're experienced and have strong delivery instincts, apply even if you don't meet every requirement.

title: AEC Expert Report Writer
description:
Objective

Identify an experienced AEC expert report writer who can transform complex technical findings into clear, structured, defensible reports for construction disputes, insurance claims, surety matters, and litigation.

Profile Overview

The ideal writer has direct experience preparing formal expert reports at the intersection of architecture, engineering, construction, insurance, and law.

They must be able to translate verbal explanations, site findings, and supporting evidence into professional reports suitable for attorneys, insurers, judges, juries, and technical experts. Prior expert report writing experience is essential; general technical writing experience alone is insufficient.

Scope

  • Engagement: Ongoing, as-needed contract
  • Volume: Approximately 2 reports per quarter
  • Hours: Approximately 20 hours per quarter, with flexibility for revisions
  • Report Length: 5–30 pages, potentially with extensive appendices
  • Structure: Primary technical assessment and secondary economic impact analysis, as applicable

Responsibilities

  • Develop expert reports using the IRAC framework (Issue, Rule, Analysis, Conclusion).
  • Translate expert-provided findings, verbal briefings, and technical documentation into cohesive reports.
  • Address construction defects, performance failures, noncompliance, errors and omissions, and insurance/surety claims.
  • Document schedule delays, liquidated damages, remediation costs, and economic impacts.
  • Incorporate contract documents, building codes, photographs, and supporting evidence.
  • Collaborate with the subject matter expert on drafts and revisions while preserving independent technical conclusions.
  • Adapt report structure to client-specific requirements and maintain strict confidentiality.

Skills and Qualifications

  • Required: Demonstrated experience writing formal AEC expert reports for insurance, surety, construction disputes, or litigation.
  • Strong knowledge of construction practices, engineering principles, and technical documentation.
  • Familiarity with IRAC and evidence-based expert reporting.
  • Ability to communicate complex findings accurately and efficiently.
  • Preferred: Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), or forensic/construction claims consulting background.
  • Experience in civil or mechanical engineering, construction delay analysis, and remediation cost assessments.

About the Client

The client is a specialized AEC professional providing forensic investigations, technical assessments, and expert consulting for complex construction, insurance, and litigation matters. They require an experienced writing partner who prioritizes accuracy, efficiency, confidentiality, and high-quality deliverables.

title: Full Stack Engineer
description:
Wynagrodzenie
umowa o pracę: 20000 – 28000 PLN / mies. brutto

We’re looking for a hands-on Full Stack Engineer who enjoys solving real business problems for our customers—not just shipping features. You’ll work closely with customers and colleagues across Coople to understand how the product is used and where the real challenges are. You’ll help decide what to build, deliver the solution, and check whether it made a difference. Most of our code is AI-generated, and you’ll guide, review, and own it in production.

This is a hybrid position in Warsaw (2 days per week on-site) in which you’ll work across our stack (Nest.js, Next.js, React Native, Neon/Postgres, AWS), closely collaborating with PMs, product, and users. We work with a founder’s mindset: take ownership, act with urgency, and focus on the problems that matter most to our users.

Skills required

  • Strong proficiency in TypeScript is a must. Other than that we look for experience with Nest.js (backend), Next.js (frontend), React Native (mobile), Postgres/Neon, and AWS (or equivalent)

  • Java experience is a plus, but not required

  • Strong understanding of CI/CD, testing strategies, performance, security, observability, and production readiness

  • Experience delivering end-to-end functionality through small, safe, frequent changes. You own what you ship, including tests, observability, behaviour in production and you’re passionate about delevering in a better way every day.

  • Comfortable working with AI-assisted development (Claude Code) and evaluating, refining AI-generated code

  • Business and product mindset: you get close to users and operational teams to understand their needs, workflows, and constraints. You turn that context into a clearly framed problem, prioritize by impact, make pragmatic trade-offs, and use evidence to check whether the solution worked. You measure success by the problems solved—not the number of features shipped

  • Adaptability and a drive to improve: you actively seek feedback, absorb new context quickly, and change course when the evidence calls for it. You take responsibility for turning lessons from delivery — what worked and what didn’t — into better engineering practices for yourself and the rest of the team

  • Fluent English and ability to commute to our Warsaw office are a must

Our Stack & Tools

  • Languages & Frameworks: TypeScript, Nest.js, Next.js, React Native

  • Data: Neon (Postgres), AWS RDS MySQL

  • Data Lake: Databricks, AWS

  • Cloud: AWS

  • Dev & Ops: Cursor, GitHub (Actions/PRs), Datadog

  • Productivity: Linear, Notion

Salary & benefits

  • PLN 20'000 – 28'000 monthly base salary (employment contract, on request we can consider B2B too)

  • On top of the base salary, we offer a yearly bonus (10% target bonus) and a company stock options plan for all employees (ESOP)

  • A healthcare service package (Lux Med) and sports membership

  • Hybrid working model: 2 days per week on-site in our office in the heart of Warsaw (next to metro Centrum / PKiN) is a must

Join a growing, multidisciplinary healthcare and behavioral health practice where you can focus on what matters most: providing excellent patient care.

We are seeking one or more psychologists to join our collaborative clinical team and provide high-quality, culturally responsive, patient-centered care to diverse populations across the lifespan. Psychologists who specialize in child, adolescent, adult, and elder care are welcome.

Our practice is committed to building strong community partnerships, and we are actively working in collaboration with substance abuse treatment centers, schools, and community-based organizations to expand access to mental health services, promote continuity of care, and address the divers behavioral health needs of the communities we serve.

Diversity As A Core Value. Our diverse referral base provides opportunities to work with children, adolescents, and adults, depending on your clinical interests, experience, specialty, and availability. CCCC offers a collegial environment designed to support professional growth, clinical collaboration, and long-term development.

  • Community engagement
  • Clinical education and workshops
  • Interdisciplinary consultation
  • Corporate and organizational consultation
  • Wellness initiatives
  • Leadership and management opportunities
  • Training and professional development

Scheduling Flexibility. At CCCC, we provide flexible opportunities for psychologists to develop a practice that aligns with their professional goals and lifestyle.

  • Full-time or part-time schedules
  • Remote, hybrid, or in-office service options
  • Evening and/or weekend availability

Dedicated Administrative Support. Our administrative team manages many of the operational demands of practice—including scheduling, billing, credentialing, insurance coordination, and patient support—allowing you to focus on delivering exceptional patient care.

  • Insurance credentialing, contracting, and authorization
  • Insurance billing, claims, and collections
  • Appointment scheduling and Waitlist management
  • Electronic health record support
  • Dedicated intakes, billing, and administrative staff for support
  • Office space, equipment, and routine supplies, as available

Key Clinical Responsibilities

Psychologistresponsibilities include:

  • Assessment and diagnosis — Conduct psychological evaluations, gather clinical histories, administer appropriate assessments, and develop diagnostic impressions when within their scope of practice.
  • Treatment — Provide evidence-based psychotherapy and other appropriate psychological interventions tailored to clients’ needs.
  • Treatment planning — Establish goals with clients, monitor progress, modify treatment when needed, and make referrals when another service is more appropriate.
  • Client safety — Assess and respond appropriately to risks such as suicide, self-harm, abuse, violence, or other urgent concerns, following applicable laws and professional standards.
  • Documentation — Maintain accurate, timely, and secure clinical records, including assessments, treatment plans, progress notes, and relevant communications.
  • Other responsibilities as required

Required Qualifications

  • Candidates must be independently licensed in Virginia or Maryland. Licensure in Washington, D.C. is preferred, with priority given to clinicians licensed across all jurisdictions
  • Priority consideration given to clinicians willing to serve pre-adolescent populations
  • Passion for high-quality, compassionate mental health care
  • Commitment to ongoing professional development
  • Desired experience 1-3 years
  • Must be local

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with range of diverse clientele
  • Availability during after-school hours, evenings, or weekends
  • Willingness to work a hybrid schedule (some in-person availability preferred)

How to Apply

We welcome experienced and emerging clinicians who are seeking a supportive, inclusive, and values-aligned professional home. To apply, please submit your CV/Resume and a brief cover letter.

CapitolHill Consortium for Counseling & Consultation LLC is an equal opportunity employer. We strongly encourage applications from BIPOC, LGBTQIA+ clinicians, and those from historically underrepresented backgrounds.

title: Community Resource Navigator
description:
Please note that applications for this position will close on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Any applications received after that date will not be reviewed or considered for the role.

MISSION

FamilyWorks partners with families to alleviate food insecurity and ensure they have resources and support to overcome systemic barriers to equity, build stable communities, and thrive.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Community Resource Navigator connects FamilyWorks’ participants to services that help stabilize their lives. Working in person from the Roosevelt Family Resource Center and the St. Luke’s satellite site, the Navigator performs needs assessments and refers, applies, and enrolls individuals and families in benefits, programs, and resources. This work happens during site-specific drop-in or distribution hours, programs, events, virtual settings, and at other locations. While these are the primary sites, the Navigator may also be asked to support other FamilyWorks locations as needed, including food access sites, family support program sites, school-based locations (such as Seattle Public Schools), satellite sites, and Mobile Food Pantry sites. Work locations may change based on funding availability but will remain within North Seattle.

The Navigator builds strong, positive relationships with participants, schools, community partners, and other key stakeholders, both within the agency and in the broader community. They will learn and enhance skills that promote anti-racism and cultural competency, and will take part in ongoing training to stay current on changes in benefits eligibility, processes, and tools. The Navigator reports to the Supportive Family Programs Manager and supervises volunteers as needed.

This is a full-time, non-exempt position paid at $32.69/hour. The schedule is Monday through Friday, with periodic evening and/or weekend commitments to support community engagement, events, and program operations. This position is partially grant funded.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES, RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS

The individual must be able to carry out each of these essential duties successfully. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Community Resource Navigation Key Responsibilities

  • Assist families to access referral and application processes for service or benefit programs such as Apple Health, SNAP, childcare, utility discount, locally available financial assistance, rental assistance, employment, and other programs to help families meet their basic needs.
  • Provide assessments and screen families for other eligible programs and provide application assistance when needed.
  • Accept, review, and respond to referrals from schools, healthcare providers, community organizations, government agencies, and other referral partners; conduct outreach and follow-up to connect participants with appropriate services and resources.
  • Support in community partnership building and facilitating outreach events to connect families to additional resources.
  • Create a welcoming and accessible environment for families to receive support.
  • Participate in mobile sites and community outreach events which include our school-based sites, mobile food pantries and more.
  • Work with volunteers and staff to conduct outreach for Community Resource Navigator services.
  • Collect and track data on participant service access and enrollment rates.
  • Remain up to date and trained on key processes, eligibility, and other tools to provide appropriate referrals to social services and other benefit programs. When appropriate, obtain certifications to directly offer enrollment.
  • Foster partnerships and connections with other organizations to meet peoples’ needs.

Other Key Responsibilities

  • Distribute, collect, and analyze surveys for participants who utilize FamilyWorks’ support services and outreach events.
  • Attend weekly and bi-weekly team meetings, monthly staff meetings, quarterly training courses, partnership meetings, and other meetings as required. Contribute to quarterly program reviews.
  • Work occasional evening and/or weekend hours to accommodate participant schedules and outreach events.
  • Enter, maintain, and update participant and program data in a timely, accurate, and complete manner across established data management systems; maintain required documentation and paperwork in accordance with organizational, funder, and reporting requirements.
  • Actively participate in furthering agency cultural competency goals including race and equity work.
  • Utilize multiple data management systems and databases to document participant interactions, referrals, service connections, outreach activities, and program outcomes while ensuring compliance with organizational and funder requirements.
  • Other duties as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS:

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required for this position.

  • Ability to work effectively within a diverse community of individuals and families; being culturally and linguistically competent.
  • Have experience working with individuals and families who face language barriers.
  • Commitment to equity and social justice and understanding the effects of system-based inequities on marginalized populations.
  • Ability to communicate effectively both interpersonally and in written/graphic formats.
  • Proven ability to de-escalate tense or emotionally charged situations with empathy, professionalism, and effective communication strategies; formal de-escalation training strongly preferred.
  • Possess and/or be willing to acquire engagement skills such as active and empathic listening, responsiveness, and trauma informed care.
  • Be organized, have coordination skills and pay attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain accurate records, manage data across multiple systems, and meet documentation and reporting deadlines with a high degree of attention to detail.
  • Have extensive knowledge of available social services.
  • Capable of effectively responding to participants’ needs and determining appropriate referrals.
  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion and professionalism
  • Ability to maintain focus in a complex environment.
  • Must have access to reliable transportation throughout North Seattle.


EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

  • Bi-lingual-speaking, a plus (English, Spanish, and/or other language). Bilingual candidates will be compensated at $1/hour above the posted rate.
  • Bachelor’s degree in social services, Psychology, Education or related field; or 4 years’ experience providing human services to a diverse community; or a combination of education and/or training and/or work experience which provides the ability to perform the work of the Community Resource Navigator.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in MS Office applications, database entry, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams.
  • Must be able to pass background check.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS/WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
  • Most work is done sitting at a desk or table; moderate lifting / carrying (40 lbs. or less) required.
  • May require standing, walking, bending, kneeling or reaching
  • Can work in different settings and is highly flexible.
  • Comfortable working in a shared workspace
  • Must be capable of the physical exertion required in interactions with young children.
  • Ability to work occasional evening or weekend hours to accommodate families’ schedule.

title: Private Wealth Client Associate

title: Senior Platform Software Engineer
description:
About the company

Our client is a software company.

The role

Raydar is recruiting for this role on behalf of our client. Own the internal infrastructure and developer tooling that helps engineering and research colleagues build, ship and run software with confidence. This is a hands-on, high-ownership position that blends infrastructure work, automation and machine learning operations.

What you'll do

- Design, build and maintain core infrastructure for research and production environments, including cloud compute, storage, CI/CD, observability and security.

- Develop internal developer tools, automation and shared libraries that raise productivity across teams.

- Create dependable pipelines and services that take models from early experiments through testing and into live use.

- Define and improve build, test and release workflows so work moves smoothly from prototype to production.

- Set up monitoring for system health and performance across services and pipelines.

- Work with research and product colleagues to find bottlenecks, streamline workflows and keep results repeatable.

- Contribute to infrastructure strategy and architecture as the organization grows.

Requirements

What we're looking for

- Strong technical fundamentals, including concurrency and software architecture, and comfort working with AI-assisted engineering.

- Solid backend engineering experience with Python or Go, APIs, databases and distributed systems.

- Working depth in Kubernetes and a major cloud provider.

- Practical production experience running workloads built on large language models.

- Has built a backend platform from the ground up that supports an external, customer-facing product.

- A mix of experience in large technology companies and in early-stage or research settings.

- Currently a senior or staff-level individual contributor who still codes daily and owns an entire system.

- A degree in computer science or another highly technical STEM field from a top university.

Bonus points

- Familiarity with data pipelines, job scheduling or machine learning experimentation workflows.

- A track record of taking product infrastructure from nothing to substantial scale.

Benefits

Compensation and benefits

- Base salary: USD 200,000 to 300,000 per year

- Equity

Location and work model

- Palo Alto, CA, United States

- On-site, 5 days per week in office

- Full-time

title: Project Coordinator
description:
Total Comp: $40,000 - $60,000 Yearly (base + bonus)
Location: Overland Park, KS
Company: DataMap
Client Work:

About DataMap

DataMap.ai is an AI-first technology consulting and solutions company focused on enterprise systems and automation. We build applications, implement ERP platforms, and provide managed services and production support at scale. Our clients include Fortune 500 enterprises and high-growth companies such as Google. They rely on us to modernize operations and automate workflows in ways that produce measurable business value.

DataMap is growing fast. We value innovation and collaboration, we work with urgency, and we reward speed, precision, and accountability. Teams here have the authority to solve complex enterprise problems and deliver results.

Why Join DataMap

At DataMap, projects run the way we expect every project to run in five years, with AI copilots drafting plans, surfacing risks, and writing first-draft status reports. Your job is to keep that setup running while you learn project management from the inside. AI tools handle the routine drafting, which leaves you more time for judgment, communication, and follow-through, and for checking every AI draft before it reaches your project manager.

You'll work alongside project managers, functional consultants, and DataMap leadership on every type of work we run, so you learn from the people whose jobs you're training for.

Role Overview

As a Project Coordinator, you'll support the project managers on your assigned projects. Project management at DataMap owns the management of all of our work, which covers everything: customer work, partner work, partnership growth, internal projects, and operations projects. Projects range from implementations of partner platforms for enterprise clients and development of the products and customer portals we build and sell (Positron, RoboApprover, Itemova EDI SaaS) to the partnership-growth, internal, and operations projects that make DataMap run and grow.

You keep the project record and logistics current (schedules, action items, documentation, and meeting cadence) so your project managers can focus on delivery and the client. You work independently on assigned tasks, collaborate as part of a team, and escalate to the project manager for guidance. Business development and commercial conversations stay with the project managers you support.

You will use AI tools every day, and we'll train you on DataMap's AI-first delivery playbook.

Your Growth Path

Project management at DataMap has a defined five-level ladder that runs from delivery support to leading the practice: Project Coordinator, Senior Project Coordinator, Project Manager, Senior Project Manager, and Director of Project Management. We post every level and promote from within, and moving up depends on performance and on the needs of the business. Beyond the Director level, the path continues into executive leadership, such as DataMap's Vice President, Operations & Delivery.

This is the support seat: you learn delivery by keeping real projects of every type running, with guidance from project managers, Senior Project Coordinators, and consultants. Strong Project Coordinators can grow into Senior Project Coordinator, where they coordinate independently across multiple projects, run delegated workstreams end to end, and mentor newer coordinators. The step after that is Project Manager, where the job moves from supporting the work to managing it. Project Managers go after business development on the projects they are on: they identify leads for new software and service sales, draft the orders, and get customer signatures. They lead their project teams: they proactively engage team members, ask what they're working on, suggest course corrections, and drive business outcomes. Along the way you work on Fortune 500 client engagements and build AI-first skills that carry into every level.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support project managers across customer, partner, partnership-growth, internal, and operations work by tracking schedules, dependencies, action items, and meeting cadence.
  • Maintain the project record (project plans, trackers, action-item logs, RAID logs, and documentation) with version control, so every team works from one source of truth.
  • Schedule meetings, prepare agendas, and capture actions and decisions with AI meeting-capture tools, then verify them and follow up with each owner until they close.
  • Consolidate project updates into first-draft weekly and monthly status reports with AI, and check each draft before the project manager reviews it.
  • Track milestones, deliverables, and governance checkpoints, flag slips early, and escalate missing inputs, issues, and risks to the project manager for guidance.
  • Log new work requests in the project record for the project manager to triage.
  • Support workshops and user acceptance testing sessions with logistics, materials, and follow-up.
  • Coordinate team onboarding, access requests, and communication among team members, functional consultants, and client and partner contacts.
  • Apply DataMap's AI-first delivery playbook (meeting capture, first-draft reporting, prompt libraries, workflow templates, and automation patterns) in your daily work.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience.
  • 0 to 2 years of experience in project coordination, administration, or IT project support (new graduates with strong internships welcome).
  • Demonstrated daily use of AI assistants (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot) in real work. Come ready to show us examples.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and problem-solving ability.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • You're adaptable, curious, and positive, and you do your best work in a fast-moving consulting environment.
  • A desire to master the project management craft.

Preferred Experience

  • CAPM or Google Project Management Professional Certificate.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office and Google Workspace (formerly G Suite); Jira and Smartsheet experience a plus.
  • Exposure to AI-powered project management features (Jira AI, Smartsheet AI, Microsoft Copilot).
  • Knowledge of business process analysis, user acceptance testing, and effective meeting management.
  • Familiarity with ERP or cloud software implementations.

Benefits & Perks

  • Total compensation of base salary plus bonus.
  • Unlimited vacation and a flexible work environment.
  • Free catered lunch on Fridays at headquarters.
  • On-site gym at headquarters.
  • 401(k) with employer match.
  • Health insurance with generous employer contribution.
  • Dental, life, and disability insurance.
  • Hands-on mentorship and career development opportunities.

Why Apply?

  • Build your career in enterprise technology consulting.
  • Support projects that run on AI copilots and major financial and supply chain systems, and help deliver AI programs for enterprise clients.
  • Work at a company that values innovation, collaboration, and professional growth.

If you're eager to learn and grow, apply even if you don't meet every requirement.

title: Cloud Solutions Architect (AWS)
description:
Wynagrodzenie

umowa o pracę: 19000 – 26200 PLN / godz. brutto

AWS Cloud Solutions Architect (AWS Batch, HPC, CPU/GPU)

Do firmy technologicznej i badawczo-rozwojowej poszukujemy osoby na stanowisko AWS Cloud Solutions Architect, która dołączy do zespołu odpowiedzialnego za rozwój i utrzymanie infrastruktury chmurowej dla klienta z branży geosciences z siedzibą w Houston.
Klient wykorzystuje środowisko AWS do realizacji zaawansowanych obliczeń naukowych, obejmujących przetwarzanie równoległe z wykorzystaniem instancji CPU i GPU. Poszukiwana osoba będzie odpowiedzialna za rozwój i automatyzację istniejącej infrastruktury oraz wsparcie zespołów klienta w bieżących zadaniach technicznych. Rola obejmuje również udział w planowaniu i projektowaniu rozwiązań architektonicznych, a także bezpośrednią współpracę z klientem i zespołem doświadczonych inżynierów AWS.

  • Tryb pracy: 100% zdalnie z terenu Polski.

  • Godziny pracy: 5 dni w tygodniu, z elastycznym początkiem dnia i dostępnością do godz. 19:00.

  • Forma współpracy: umowa B2B lub umowa o pracę.

  • Klient: firma z USA działająca w branży geosciences.

  • Języki: polski i angielski- komunikacja z klientem odbywa się w języku angielskim.

Czym będziesz się zajmować?

• Projektowaniem i rozwijaniem infrastruktury AWS wykorzystywanej do obliczeń równoległych, w tym konfiguracją AWS Batch (kolejki, definicje zadań, automatyczne skalowanie) oraz doborem instancji CPU, GPU i memory-optimized.
• Automatyzacją wdrażania i zarządzania infrastrukturą z wykorzystaniem Terraform, CloudFormation oraz skryptów w Pythonie.
• Konfiguracją i zabezpieczaniem środowiska sieciowego AWS, w tym VPC, podsieci, Security Groups, VPC Endpoints oraz uprawnień IAM i permission boundaries.
• Zarządzaniem danymi i dostępem do nich w Amazon S3, również pomiędzy różnymi kontami AWS, oraz pracą ze środowiskami kontenerowymi Docker, ECR i ECS.
• Monitorowaniem działania infrastruktury, analizą jej wykorzystania i optymalizacją kosztów z użyciem CloudWatch i Athena, a także obsługą kolejek i powiadomień za pomocą SQS i SNS.
• Wdrażaniem i wspieraniem rozwiązań w środowiskach DEV, TEST i PROD oraz współpracą z zespołami odpowiedzialnymi za cloud operations, bezpieczeństwo, sieć, storage i rozwój oprogramowania.
• Analizowaniem potrzeb użytkowników, doradztwem w zakresie architektury rozwiązań chmurowych oraz przygotowywaniem dokumentacji technicznej w Azure DevOps Wiki.

Czego oczekujemy?

Wymagania konieczne:
• Bardzo dobrej znajomości AWS, w szczególności w zakresie bezpieczeństwa, konfiguracji sieci oraz utrzymania i zarządzania infrastrukturą chmurową.
• Praktycznego doświadczenia w realizacji obliczeń równoległych z wykorzystaniem procesorów CPU i GPU.
• Praktycznej znajomości AWS Batch, w tym konfiguracji kolejek zadań i automatycznego skalowania zasobów.
• Doświadczenia w pracy z Terraform oraz podejściem Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
• Dobrej znajomości Pythona, w szczególności w zakresie automatyzacji wdrożeń i zarządzania usługami AWS.
• Znajomości języka angielskiego umożliwiającej codzienną komunikację z klientem z USA oraz znajomości języka polskiego.
• Samodzielności, proaktywnego podejścia do rozwiązywania problemów oraz umiejętności komunikacji z zespołami technicznymi i biznesowymi.
Mile widziane:

• Znajomość CloudFormation oraz Python CDK.
• Doświadczenie w pracy z technologiami kontenerowymi: Docker, ECR i ECS.

title: Senior Business Analyst
description:
Senior Business Analyst


The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is hiring a Senior Business Analyst within the Financial Stability Institute.


Application deadline: Please note that the deadline for applications is 20 November 2026 at the end of day.


Please note that this role is offered as a 3-year fixed term contract.


This role is based in Basel, Switzerland; however, thanks to our status as an international organization, we can hire globally and welcome applications from candidates of all nationalities and located anywhere in the world. Relocation support is available for the successful candidate and their dependent family members.


Purpose of the job:


Serve as a central coordination point for the successful implementation the FSI’s Capacity Development Modernisation (CDM) project as part of the BIS’ medium-term strategy - BIS100. The CDM aims to future-proof the FSI’s capacity development (CD) offering through more interactive e-learning content, AI-enabled learning experience and platform interoperability to better support financial authorities globally.

This position is expected to undertake the CDM project management and leverage the latest e-learning market developments building upon the Bank’s technological infrastructure and the FSI’s capacity development ecosystem (eg FSI Connect and online courses).

This position also operates as a key liaison between the FSI and internal/external stakeholders, including the Strategic Project Management Office (SPMO) and vendors, to ensure that the CDM project is delivered in accordance with its approved scope, budget, milestones, governance requirements and expected project outcomes.

.

By joining the Financial Stability Institute team, you will:

  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to simplify processes, improve efficiency and enhance performance.
  • Contribute to delivering successful initiatives, ensuring that solutions are aligned with organisational priorities and deliver measurable value
  • Benefit from working in a unique, international environment that offers flexible, hybrid working options with a blend of onsite work from our central office location in Basel and home office.

Principal Accountabilities:

  • With subject matter experts, define and analyse CDM requirements, identify potential solutions by collaborating closely within the FSI and other teams to determine what's feasible, considering technical limitations, budget constraints, and timeframes.
  • Act as the principal operational contact for the strategic project management office, responding to requests for information and coordinating the preparation of project updates, governance papers and other required submissions.
  • Maintain and update the project plan, including milestones, deliverables, dependencies, resources, critical-path activities and decision points; monitor progress and escalate delays or emerging delivery issues.
  • Monitor the CDM budget and financial position, including approved budgets, actual and committed expenditure, forecasts, variances and prepare regular financial updates.
  • Coordinate with external suppliers, consultants, platform providers, implementation partners and academic institutions, administering procurement, invoicing and contract management, monitoring deliverables, milestones, acceptance criteria, costs, invoices, risks and contractual obligations.
  • Contribute to stakeholder engagement: finding out their needs, issues, and concerns particularly from the pilot evaluations; reacting to these needs, issues, and concerns; arranging meetings and events; and drafting supporting materials to promote understanding and commitment.
  • Carry out feasibility and assessment work for proposed and current projects to contribute to the development and continuous review of business cases.
  • Contribute to reviewing existing operations and generate new ideas to assist in identifying continuous improvements, particularly with respect to streamlining and optimising operations.
  • Support specific technology implementation processes such as the use of AI on content development, platform interoperability and AI features on the learning platfom. Define and coordinate testing and acceptance activities for new content, AI-enabled functionality, platform enhancements and interoperability, ensuring that implementation issues are recorded, prioritised and resolved. Work closely with developers and testers to resolve issues, ensure that the solution aligns with business goals and objectives.
  • Develop and monitor standard business performance metrics for the CDM project within the organisation's established systems to deliver required insights for decision making.

Qualifications, skills and experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent level. Master’s degree or other relevant postgraduate degree or specialisation would be an asset.
  • Experience with learning-management systems, digital learning, or technology-enabled business transformation. Experience with artificial intelligence will be an asset.
  • Experience coordinating cross-functional projects from feasibility and planning through implementation and transition to business as usual.
  • Experience conducting gap analysis between current and future states to identify components of the overall change strategy.
  • Understands business context, needs, rules, and technological architecture, as well as organisational structure, cultures, capabilities, and processes to document business operations.
  • Ability to lead facilitated sessions for requirements elicitation, focus groups, and user acceptance testing.
  • Experiened to express user needs in terms of business requirements, identify current capability of the business to deliver, conduct build or buy analyses, and recommend preferred approach.
  • Experienced to assess process performance and to recommend improvements.
  • Experienced to prioritise components of a project, programme, or portfolio work in context with risks, activities, stakeholders, etc. across the life of the project or programme.
  • Ability to identify potential stakeholders, analyse their expectations, and develop strategies for managing stakeholders and their expectations.
  • Experienced to manage the documentation, archiving, traceability, changes, and approvals of requirements throughout the project life cycle.
  • Experienced to coordinate and collaborate effectively with colleagues to obtain information, feedback and input on key deliverables of the project.
  • Demonstrated attention to detail and commitment to maintaining accurate and reliable project records.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and meet fixed reporting deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Please note that the BIS's corporate language is English, which is used for all internal and external communication.


Who we are:

Internationalism is at the core of our identity and the best representation of this is our workforce. With employees from over 66 countries and offices in nine locations, the BIS is a global organisation with a truly international workforce. By joining us, you will work in a unique, highly rewarding, and international work environment. We are committed to equal opportunities at the BIS and aim to build a workforce that reflects our global membership. We strive to attract the best talent and foster an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, including those with a breadth of professional experience. You can discover more about our inclusive working environment here.



What the BIS offers:

We want your time at BIS to be a rewarding and career-enriching experience. We offer an agile and flexible working environment with hybrid working opportunities including home office and working from abroad days. To support our international applicants, we offer relocation support that extends to your dependent family members. In addition, we offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, including support for working families including childcare and education allowances (where applicable). Finally, we offer a genuinely unique international working environment, which will give you exposure to the global financial system and the opportunity to collaborate with passionate experts from all over the world.

title: Head of Partnerships & Brand Sponsorships
description:
Position Overview

Contrarian Thinking is a media, advisory, and investment firm on a mission to take back Main Street. We don't just talk about business. We advise it, we invest in it, and we broadcast it to an audience that actually trusts us.

Three businesses, one flywheel:

  • Media: Contrarian Thinking and Codie Sanchez's podcasts, YouTube, newsletter, books, social, and live events, built to be the most trusted business media brand in the world.
  • Advisory: Our communities, advisors, and curriculum help owners, buyers, and builders buy, scale, and sell businesses the smart way.
  • Investment: We put our own capital to work, buying and backing Main Street businesses and helping them scale into enduring, profitable companies.

Media earns the attention. Advisory earns the trust. Investment puts skin in the game. That combination is why brands want in, and it's the platform you'll be selling.

We're looking for a Head of Partnerships & Sponsorships to own every dollar of brand, sponsorship, and partnership revenue across all Contrarian Thinking and Codie Sanchez media assets, and to build it into an 8-figure business.

This role is responsible for building the sponsorship strategy and rate card, selling and closing category partners, running deals from first pitch through renewal, and building the team and systems to scale it.

This role sits at the intersection of Media & Content, Events & Community, Marketing, and Finance. You'll work closely with content leads and producers, the events team, and leadership to make sure partnerships make the content better, not worse.

We're past #ad reads and #sponsoredposts, and you are too. You'll sell story-driven, multi-touch partnerships that brands want to be part of and our audience actually trusts. You'll start as a player-coach: closing the first deals yourself, then hiring and leading the team as the department grows.

What You'll Own

Sponsorship & partnership strategy

  • Define how we package and sell sponsorships across all Contrarian Thinking and Codie Sanchez media assets: podcast, YouTube, newsletter, social, live events, and community
  • Build the packaging, rate card, inventory calendar, and brand-safety guardrails
  • Own the plan and annual targets to build an 8-figure partnerships & sponsorships business

Selling & closing

  • Build and work a pipeline of category partners (e.g. finance, travel, auto, lifestyle, business tools)
  • Pitch big-idea creative concepts to brand-side VPs, CMOs, and their agencies; negotiate and close
  • Sell the team internally on ideas before they ever go to a brand

Partner execution & renewal

  • Shepherd deals from signed contract through campaign delivery, reporting, and renewal
  • Protect creative integrity and our voice in review cycles without torching the relationship
  • Report partnership ROI back to partners and to leadership

Affiliate & community partnerships

  • Vet and manage partners that offer real value to our Buyers and Builders communities
  • Grow affiliate and referral programs that align with our mission

Team, systems & data

  • Build the CRM pipeline, contracts process, and dashboards (pipeline, booked vs. delivered revenue, partner ROI, renewal rate)
  • Hire and lead the partnerships team as revenue grows
  • Report weekly to the President on pipeline, booked revenue, and delivery

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days

  • Full audit of current and past sponsors, inventory, and pricing across every property; recommendation on what to sell and at what price
  • Rate card, pitch deck, and partnership one-pager approved by leadership
  • A qualified pipeline of category prospects built in the CRM, with the first category deals closed or in contract
  • Standing weekly rhythm with Content, Events, and Finance so inventory and delivery are never a surprise

First year

  • Build an 8-figure partnerships & sponsorships business across all Contrarian Thinking and Codie Sanchez media assets
  • Multiple signed 7-figure category partnerships structured for multi-year renewal
  • Partner-integrated content matches or outperforms non-sponsored content on retention and engagement
  • Strong partner renewals and a repeatable process the next hire can run

What We're Looking For

  • 8-10+ years in brand partnerships, sponsorship sales, or business development at a creator-led media company, publisher, agency, or events business, including leading a sponsorship revenue function at scale
  • A track record of personally closing 7-figure brand deals and owning 8-figure partnership revenue, ideally category partnerships rather than one-offs
  • Existing relationships with brand-side marketing leaders and agencies
  • Experience building a sponsorship function from scratch: packaging, pricing, process, and team
  • Strong negotiator with a diplomatic spine; you can say "we won't do that" to a brand without drama
  • Comfortable in data: CRM, platform analytics, and partner reporting
  • Clear, concise writer of pitches and briefs
  • Low ego, high standards, bias toward action

What Makes You Stand Out

  • Experience selling across podcast, YouTube, newsletter, and live events in one package
  • You've hired and led a partnerships or sales team
  • You use AI tools as a thinking multiplier for research, pitching, and reporting
  • Interest in small business, acquisitions, and entrepreneurship

Who You Are

  • You're the person at the party who introduces two strangers and watches them hit it off
  • Show me your results, not your intentions
  • Winners want pressure; you like owning a number
  • Better weird than boring; you bring ideas, not templates
  • You do the dirty work and close the loop

Why This Role Matters

  • Most media companies treat brand partnerships as a tax on audience attention. We're building the opposite: partnerships that make the content better and fund more of it.
  • This role turns our audience reach into a durable, diversified revenue line for the company.

Location

Austin, TX - Full time in office. Applicants must live within a 1-hour drive of Austin or be willing to relocate.

Type of Employment

Full-Time. Reports to the President.

Crew Benefits

  • 100% Company-paid health, dental, and vision for all full-time Crew Members with an option to add any dependents.
  • Unlimited PTO Policy (with approval from your Direct Support) + 8 paid US holidays
  • On-time direct deposit pay 2x/month
  • Option to enroll in a 401(k) plan via Vestwell with competitive match options
  • Learn expert deal-making and how to buy businesses with 100% free access to all of our courses and our flagship Contrarian Community

How To Apply

Include a resume plus a short Loom walking us through a brand partnership or sponsorship you closed that you're proud of: the creative idea, the deal structure, how it performed, and your role from pitch to renewal.

title: Director of Change Management
description:
Total Comp: $120,000 - $180,000 Yearly (base + bonus)
Also Known As: Head of Organizational Change Management
Location: Overland Park, KS
Workplace: In person (not remote)
Company: DataMap
Client Work:

About DataMap

DataMap.ai is an AI-first technology consulting and solutions company focused on enterprise systems and automation. We build applications, implement ERP platforms, and provide managed services and production support at scale. Our clients include Fortune 500 enterprises and high-growth companies such as Google. They rely on us to modernize operations and automate workflows in ways that produce measurable business value.

DataMap is growing fast. We value innovation and collaboration, we work with urgency, and we reward speed, precision, and accountability. Teams here have the authority to solve complex enterprise problems and deliver results.

Summary

Ready to lead DataMap's change management practice?

Every platform DataMap implements and every product we build changes how people work, and the change pays off only when they adopt it. As the Director of Change Management, you lead the practice that owns the people side of everything DataMap runs: rollouts of the partner platforms we implement (Coupa, D365, NetSuite, SAP, and Boomi), adoption of our own products (Positron, RoboApprover, Itemova EDI SaaS), and change inside DataMap as the firm grows. You are accountable for adoption across the portfolio and for the methodology, governance, and measurement the practice runs on, and you set the practice's direction with DataMap's executive leadership. This role is in person at DataMap's office in Overland Park, Kansas, and is not remote.

Change management is a career path at DataMap, from Change Manager to Senior Change Manager to Director of Change Management. Beyond the Director level, the path continues into executive leadership, such as DataMap's Vice President, Operations & Delivery. We promote from within, and moving up depends on performance and on the needs of the business.

Your Role and Responsibilities

Practice leadership and methodology

  • Build and maintain DataMap's change methodology as one playbook, with a standard toolkit every change manager uses: stakeholder maps that sort each group into Allies, Opponents, Neutrals, and Adversaries, impact and readiness assessments, WIIFM messaging, communication and feedback plans, and RACI matrices.
  • Make training and third-party change part of the methodology and offerings: one approach to training needs analysis, curriculum, train-the-trainer programs, and proficiency measurement, plus playbooks for onboarding suppliers and customers and for working with other implementation service providers on shared programs.
  • Set change governance (readiness criteria, adoption gates, and post-go-live sustainment checks) and the practice's measurement standard for adoption, proficiency, third-party enablement, and business results.
  • Lead the AI transformation of the change practice with the executive team, covering tool selection, methodology changes, and ROI measurement.

Executive and stakeholder engagement

  • Represent the people side on executive steering committees, advise C-level sponsors, and be the escalation point for adoption risk and resistance across the portfolio, bringing executive leadership in when needed.
  • Drive change inside DataMap as the firm scales, in process, structure, visibility, communications, and change management, using the same playbook the practice runs for clients.
  • Present DataMap's AI-first approach to change in client executive briefings and industry content, working with Sales.

Team and practice growth

  • Build the change management team: hiring, the career path, certification paths, standards, and culture.
  • Develop the practice's next generation of change leaders, and coach them to engage their champion networks often, ask what they're seeing, and correct course early.
  • Grow change, training, and adoption work across DataMap's accounts, and contribute to the pricing and packaging of change, training, supplier and customer enablement, and adoption services.

Education and Experience

  • At least 10 years of experience in change management or transformation, including building, leading, and developing teams of change managers.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • Experience building a change methodology, governance, and measurement approach that others run, and a track record of organization-level change that held after launch.
  • Experience leading training at scale and change that reaches beyond the organization to suppliers, customers, and other implementation service providers.
  • Executive presence, with experience advising C-level sponsors, sitting on steering committees, and leading leaders outside your reporting line.
  • Commercial experience growing change and adoption work, including input to pricing and packaging.
  • A track record of bringing AI into a change practice or delivery organization and measuring the return.
  • Ability to work in person at DataMap's office in Overland Park, Kansas. This role is not remote.
  • Knowledge of established change models, especially Lewin's change model and Kotter's 8 steps, as well as Prosci's ADKAR model, the Bridges Transition Model, the McKinsey 7-S Framework, or force field analysis, is a plus. Prosci or CCMP certification is a strong plus.
  • Consulting or professional services experience, and change leadership on SaaS or ERP transformations (such as Coupa, NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or Microsoft Dynamics 365), are a plus.

Benefits & Perks

  • Total compensation of base salary plus bonus.
  • Unlimited vacation and a flexible work environment.
  • Free catered lunch on Fridays at headquarters.
  • On-site gym at headquarters.
  • 401(k) with employer match.
  • Health insurance with generous employer contribution.
  • Dental, life, and disability insurance.
  • Hands-on mentorship and career development opportunities.

If you're experienced and have strong change leadership instincts, apply even if you don't meet every requirement.

title: Research Intern - Office of Applied Research
description:
Overview

Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment.


The Office of Applied Research in Microsoft seeks research interns to conduct state-of-the-art applied research. Applied research is impact-driven research. It applies empirical techniques to real world problems in a way that transforms theory into reality, advancing the state-of-the-art in the process.

The Office of Applied Research brings together experts in frontier Artificial Intelligence (AI) model development and human-centered AI to tackle real-world challenges at scale in the enterprise AI space. We work closely with research and product partners to ensure Microsoft is advancing cutting-edge research aligned with our core product interests.

Ideal candidates have proven experience in various fields such as Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Reinforcement Learning (RL), Learning from human feedback and Human-centered AI. We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in areas such as reinforcement learning and model mid- and post-training, continual learning, differential privacy, human-AI collaboration, or the development and evaluation of enterprise AI agents, including learning from user feedback in real-world deployments.



Responsibilities

Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer.



Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Information Science, Statistics, Information Systems, Economics, Operation Research or a related STEM field.

Other Requirements

  • Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship.
  • In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 1+ year(s) of experience in conducting research and writing peer-reviewed publications.
  • Ability to think unconventionally to derive creative and innovative solutions.
  • Actively conducting research in at least one of the following areas:
    • Collaborative or Multi-party AI Agents (e.g. AI teammates)
    • Mid- and post-training for LLMs / Agents
    • Learning from user interaction or feedback
    • Synthetic data generation for LLM evaluation and fine-tuning
    • Understanding, verifying, or evaluating LLMs outputs
    • Differential privacy for LLM and data
    • Continual Learning / Test-time Training
    • Agents (e.g. Memory, Goal management, Inter-Agent conversations)
    • Multi Agent Simulations (e.g. evaluating or training AI agents in collaborative settings)
    • Forward deployment for enterprise AI
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with your mentor and others in Microsoft on research projects.
  • Demonstrated interpersonal and communication skills, cross-group, and cross-culture collaboration skills.

The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month.

Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here:

Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April).


This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.



Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances.
